subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On the H–R diagram, where is the Sun and most of the lifetime of stars spent?
questions.explain: Stars spend most of their lives fusing hydrogen on the main sequence, the diagonal band where the Sun lies.

questions.q: How many photons of wavelength 600 nm are needed to deliver 1.0 J of energy? (E ≈ 3.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ J per photon)
questions.explain: Number = total energy / photon energy = 1.0 / 3.3×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 3.0×10¹⁸ photons.

questions.q: In an astronomical refracting telescope in normal adjustment, what is the role of the objective lens?
options: To increase the field of view only
To correct chromatic aberration in the eyepiece
To produce a magnified virtual image for the eye
To form a real image of a distant object at its focal point
questions.explain: The objective forms a real, inverted image of the distant object at its focal point, which the eyepiece then magnifies.

questions.q: The energy of a photon of frequency f is given by:
questions.explain: Photon energy E = hf, where h is the Planck constant.

questions.q: The parallax angle p of a star (in arcseconds) is related to its distance d (in parsecs) by:
questions.explain: By definition of the parsec, distance in parsecs equals the reciprocal of the parallax angle in arcseconds.

questions.q: In the standard OBAFGKM spectral classification, which sequence is ordered from hottest to coolest?
options: G, F, A, B, O, K, M
O, B, A, F, G, K, M
A, B, O, F, G, K, M
M, K, G, F, A, B, O
questions.explain: The spectral sequence O B A F G K M runs from the hottest (O) to the coolest (M) stars.

questions.q: A key advantage of a reflecting telescope over a large refracting telescope is that the reflector:
options: always has a larger field of view
does not suffer from chromatic aberration
has no spherical aberration at all
questions.explain: Mirrors reflect all wavelengths identically, so reflectors avoid the chromatic aberration that affects lenses.

questions.q: A metal has a work function of 2.0 eV. What is the threshold frequency? (1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s)
If the speed of an electron is increased, its de Broglie wavelength:
questions.explain: Since λ = h/p and p = mv, increasing speed increases momentum and therefore decreases the wavelength.

questions.q: Why must X-ray and most ultraviolet telescopes be placed on satellites above the atmosphere?
options: Because the atmosphere absorbs X-ray and most UV radiation
Because radio dishes interfere with them at ground level
Because these telescopes need zero gravity to focus
Because the atmosphere magnifies these wavelengths too much
questions.explain: The atmosphere is opaque to X-rays and most UV, so such telescopes must operate in space.

questions.q: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by the wave model of light mainly because the wave model predicts:
options: Instant emission at all frequencies given enough intensity
questions.explain: The wave model predicts any frequency could eventually free electrons with enough intensity/time, contradicting the observed threshold frequency.

questions.q: A graph of maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons against frequency has a gradient equal to:
questions.explain: From KEmax = hf − φ, the gradient of KEmax against f is the Planck constant h.

questions.q: According to the Rayleigh criterion, two point sources are just resolved by a telescope of aperture D at wavelength λ when their angular separation is approximately:
questions.explain: The Rayleigh criterion for a circular aperture gives the minimum resolvable angle θ ≈ 1.22 λ/D.

questions.q: The Schwarzschild radius of a black hole marks the:
options: radius of its visible accretion disc
distance at which planets can orbit safely
event horizon, the boundary from within which not even light can escape
questions.explain: The Schwarzschild radius defines the event horizon, the surface from inside which the escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.

questions.q: After a massive star explodes as a supernova, the dense remnant left behind is a neutron star or, if massive enough:
questions.explain: If the collapsing core exceeds the neutron-star mass limit, gravity overwhelms all support and a black hole forms.

questions.q: One electronvolt (1 eV) is equal to:
questions.explain: 1 eV is the energy gained by an electron accelerated through 1 V, equal to 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ J.

questions.q: In a photoelectric experiment, the stopping potential V_s relates to maximum KE by:
questions.explain: The stopping potential just halts the fastest electrons, so eV_s = ½mv²max, the maximum kinetic energy.

questions.q: The double-slit experiment provided important evidence that light:
options: Behaves as a wave because it produces interference fringes
questions.explain: The interference fringes can only be explained by superposition of waves, supporting the wave nature of light.

questions.q: On a Hertzsprung–Russell diagram, the axes are conventionally:
options: luminosity against temperature, with temperature decreasing to the right
questions.explain: The H–R diagram plots luminosity (or absolute magnitude) against temperature (or spectral class), with temperature decreasing from left to right.

questions.q: Type Ia supernovae are valuable as standard candles in cosmology because they:
options: occur only in our own Galaxy
all have the same surface temperature
reach a known, consistent peak absolute magnitude
questions.explain: Type Ia supernovae have a reliably consistent peak luminosity, so their apparent brightness gives their distance.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by:
questions.explain: The de Broglie wavelength is λ = h/p, where p is the particle's momentum.

questions.q: Why does photoelectric emission occur almost instantaneously when light above the threshold frequency strikes a metal?
options: A single photon delivers all its energy to one electron at once
questions.explain: A photon transfers its energy to a single electron in one interaction, so emission is essentially instantaneous.

questions.q: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on:
options: The intensity of the incident light
The frequency of the incident light
The size of the metal plate
questions.explain: Max KE = hf − φ, so it depends on the frequency of the light, not the intensity.

questions.q: A string of length 1.2 m fixed at both ends vibrates in its fundamental (first harmonic) mode. The wavelength is:
questions.explain: The fundamental has one antinode and length = λ/2, so λ = 2 × 1.2 = 2.4 m.

questions.q: Which harmonics are present in a pipe closed at one end?
questions.explain: A closed pipe supports only odd harmonics (1st, 3rd, 5th...) because of the node-antinode boundary conditions.

questions.q: Star A appears blue-white and star B appears red. Which is correct?
options: B is hotter and peaks at a shorter wavelength than A
A is cooler because blue light has lower energy
A is hotter and peaks at a shorter wavelength than B
questions.explain: By Wien's law a hotter star peaks at a shorter (bluer) wavelength, so the blue-white star A is hotter.

questions.q: Two stars have the same surface temperature, but star X is four times the radius of star Y. The luminosity of X compared with Y is:
questions.explain: With temperature equal, L ∝ A ∝ r², so four times the radius gives 4² = 16 times the luminosity.

questions.q: In an electron diffraction tube, increasing the accelerating voltage causes the diffraction rings to:
questions.explain: Higher voltage gives electrons greater momentum and shorter de Broglie wavelength, so the diffraction rings shrink.

questions.q: The quantum efficiency of a CCD refers to:
options: the fraction of incident photons that liberate a detectable electron
the ratio of focal length to aperture
the number of pixels in the detector
questions.explain: Quantum efficiency is the fraction of incident photons that produce a stored charge, and for CCDs it is far higher (~70–90%) than for the eye or film.

questions.q: For a refracting telescope in normal adjustment, the angular magnification is given by which expression?
questions.explain: Angular magnification M = fo/fe, the ratio of the objective focal length to the eyepiece focal length.
